subject: CALL statement
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB237). "If the NESTED phrase is not specified, program-prototype-name-1 is used to determine the characteristics of the called program." All three characteristics the rule reaches are now taken from the prototype. (a) THE EXTERNALIZED PROGRAM-NAME: BindCall sets literalName from ProgramPrototype.ExternalizedName when neither identifier-1 nor literal-1 is written (GR3 b) third bullet), and 12.3.8.4 GR10 NOTE 1 decides which name that is - literal-3 if the specifier wrote AS, else the prototype name. (b) THE SIGNATURE for SR14/SR25: BuildProgramDefinitionTable is the compilation group's outermost program definitions keyed by externalized name - 12.3.8.4 GR10 a)'s search space - and a hit supplies the CalleeSignature that every 14.8.2/14.8.3 check in BindCall reads. A miss is GR10 c), the external repository, which for this implementation is the run unit's program registry resolved at activation (14.9.4.4 GR3 b)), so a separately-compiled callee stays legal and simply carries no compile-time signature. (c) THE BY REFERENCE/BY VALUE MODE OF EACH FORMAL that GR9 consults: the keyword-less-argument arm reads calleeFormals[pos].ByValue, which is now populated for a prototype call exactly as for AS NESTED - the golden's SCALE-IT call passes a bare argument to a BY VALUE formal and GR9 b) selects BY VALUE, observably leaving the argument unchanged (14.2.3 GR10). The negative pins the signature actually being USED: two arguments against a one-formal callee draws COBOL1684 (14.8.2.1) at bind, quoting `CALL ... program-prototype 'ARG-PROTO'`.
